resources.string:
When the app is closed, your address stays online. Your contacts can write to you and call you.

Messages that arrive are stored as they are, still encrypted, and sealed a second time: they can only be opened with your PIN. Unknown people who have your link have to wait until the app is open.

A notification says only "Whospair is buzzing you": no name, no content. For a call, open Whospair, enter your PIN, then answer — your contact keeps calling for a minute.

The price: your onion key stays in memory while the app is closed, Android shows a permanent notification, your address is online around the clock, and the battery drains faster. After a restart of the phone, nothing runs until you enter your PIN.
Without this, Android may put Whospair to sleep and you will stop being reachable.
Notifications are off for Whospair: messages will still wait for your PIN, but nothing will tell you they arrived.
Android requires a \"Reachable\" notification while Whospair stays reachable. You can hide it: the service keeps running, and the state shows in the app, next to Tor.
Someone is trying to reach you
Open Whospair and enter your PIN to answer.
